analysis_notes.summary: LM2 Torah 108 is a two-line aphorism with no bechina language whatsoever. The Rebbe states that a person can lose both worlds (this world and the World to Come) for a trivial quarter-hour pleasure. The teaching contains one eitza-type relationship (תַּעֲנוּג קָטָן → אֲבֵידַת כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת: a small pleasure causes the loss of all worlds), but there are no bechina equalities of the form 'X is an aspect of Y'. No concepts are flagged as missing from the dataset because the text does not employ bechina language that would generate dataset nodes.
